Practical electrical information

Electrical Faults in Perth: Safety and What to Report

Electrical faults are best described by what is happening: a safety switch that will not stay on, lighting that has stopped working, an outlet that feels loose, or power loss in a particular area. Do not open switchboards, remove covers or test fixed wiring.

For smoke, fire, active arcing, fallen lines or electrical equipment in contact with water, move clear and call 000. For a wider network outage or hazard, follow the advice of the relevant utility.

How electrical repair work is scoped

Our Perth electrical team starts with the affected area, the observable symptom, any safe warning signs and the property access details. We use that information to identify the repair scope. Fault location, access, equipment, materials and any additional work found during assessment are confirmed in a written quote before work proceeds.

For homes, rentals, strata and commercial properties, do not attempt to diagnose from a switchboard or remove a fitting. Tell us what changed, what has been affected and whether there is a safe access contact. Our Perth team arranges a safe on-site assessment and confirms the electrical repair scope and quote.

A practical booking path

Booking an Electrician in Perth: Symptoms, Safety and Access

Describe the symptom

Say what stopped working, where it is located and what changed first. Avoid diagnosing, opening covers or testing equipment.

Flag safety concerns

Report smoke, burning smell, heat, arcing, visible damage or water near electrical equipment from a safe position.

Share access details

For rental, strata and commercial properties, include the access contact and approval pathway with the request.

Electrical Fault Finding or Installation in Perth

Fault finding establishes why existing equipment or a circuit is not working. Planned installation starts with the new fitting, its location and the existing supply. Record these as separate tasks if you need both. Vehicle electrics, refrigeration repairs and specialist energy systems are not automatically included in a household electrical enquiry. Discuss the equipment and proposed scope before purchasing a replacement or booking specialist work.

Is fault finding included in a repair price?

Investigation and repair can be different stages. Ask what assessment is included, how an unresolved or intermittent fault would be handled, and which repair or replacement work needs separate approval. The written quote should make those boundaries clear.

Should I request a switchboard upgrade when power keeps tripping?

A recurring trip does not establish that an upgrade is needed. Request an assessment of the affected installation first. Replacement or additional circuit work should follow the findings and an agreed scope, not the symptom alone.

Can I book an after-hours electrician online?

Routine service hours: 09:00–21:00, seven days a week. 24-hour emergency repairs are available; call to confirm attendance arrangements and the quoted emergency work. No arrival time is guaranteed. Call 0413 477 667 for urgent work; an online form does not reserve an appointment. For shock or network danger, use the official safety route first.

What are your routine hours and emergency arrangements?

Routine service hours: 09:00–21:00, seven days a week. 24-hour emergency repairs are available; call to confirm attendance arrangements and the quoted emergency work. No arrival time is guaranteed. Emergency repair fees follow the quoted work plan. For urgent work, call rather than relying on an online enquiry.

What household electrical work requires a licensed electrician in WA?

Arrange fixed wiring and power-point work through appropriately licensed electrical professionals and verify the relevant current documentation. Read the explanation.

Electrician costs in Perth: investigation or installation?

An electrical fault-finding visit investigates a reported problem. A planned installation quote starts with the fitting or outlet you want and the work needed at that location. Keep both tasks visible if you need an existing fault assessed as well as new equipment installed.

For a useful price comparison, check attendance, investigation, parts, electrical work and any additional access separately. Ask what happens if a fault is intermittent or the initial visit identifies further work. The published guide is not a promise of unlimited investigation, a free call-out or a fixed hourly rate.

Use the property location as well as the service when making the request. For a rental or strata building, add the access contact and the person who can approve the work. A suburb in the directory does not confirm an appointment or specialist service capability.
